column1: # Port routes: how to get from a source (loader, Minecraft) to the next stop on the way to a target.
# tools/route.py chains these rows into hops; tools/port.py runs one hop at a time, finishing each
# (compile + Gate B) before the next starts, so every hop's pack is applied to code that compiles.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   from_loader  from_mc (fnmatch glob)  to_loader  to_mc  kind  pack  setup
#   kind:  loader   change of loader (and version), from a decompiled jar
#          version  same loader, different Minecraft version family
#          era      1.21.1 -> 26.x: the multi-version frame + its rename table, flattened (CATALOG §W/§V)
#   pack:  the deterministic rewrites for the hop, or `-` when none exists yet. A hop with no pack
#          STOPS the port unless --allow-no-pack: the workers would have to do the whole hop, which is
#          exactly the expensive case, so it is a decision for the person, never a silent fallback.
#   setup: how the decompiled names are made official: srg | intermediary | none
# Add a row when a new pack lands (tools/learn-pack.py writes one). Order matters only for ties:
# the first matching row wins.
